title: How LinkedIn Trains AI Job Search 8x Faster with Multi-Teacher Distillation
gist: LinkedIn distills an 8B relevance oracle and a 1.7B engagement teacher into a 0.6B ranking model that lifted NDCG@10 by 24.48% (0.7583 to 0.9432) and raised throughput from ~290 to over 2,000 items per second per GPU, with the real contribution being a custom SGLang-based framework that serves teachers inside the training loop for a roughly 8x compound training speedup.

themes.theme: Systems work, not the technique, is the moat

insights.claim: The main contribution of LinkedIn's job search pipeline is not the distillation technique but the systems work that makes iteration fast, centred on a custom framework built on SGLang that serves teacher models directly in the training loop.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Competitive advantage in applied ML is shifting to training-loop infrastructure, which is far harder to copy than a published method.
insights.quote: The main contribution isn’t just the distillation technique. It’s the systems work that makes it fast enough for iteration.
insights.locator: LinkedIn has published details of the training infrastructure

insights.claim: The system is built on SGLang, the open-source LLM serving engine LinkedIn has already invested in for prior ranking workloads, rather than a proprietary serving stack.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Large-scale production commitment to SGLang strengthens it as a default open serving layer against vLLM-class alternatives.
insights.locator: It's built on SGLang, the open-source LLM serving engine

insights.claim: Querying one or more large teacher models for every training example makes teacher serving the bottleneck for a ranking system that must handle hundreds of thousands of queries per second.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Inference-in-the-training-loop is an under-appreciated cost centre that determines how fast a team can iterate on ranking models.
insights.locator: Training a small language model (SLM) to improve relevance

insights.claim: LinkedIn's Online Multi-teacher Distillation uses an asynchronous client to query teachers during training, process outputs and add them to the distillation losses; scaling this across several nodes with local teacher replicas accelerated distillation by 3x while keeping latency low.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Local teacher replication is a concrete 3x lever for anyone running LLM-supervised training.
insights.locator: LinkedIn created a multi-teacher distillation framework using SGLang

insights.claim: Offline Multi-teacher Distillation precomputes teacher outputs and stores them on HDFS or NFS for direct use in training, eliminating serving overhead and repeated calculation.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Caching teacher outputs converts recurring GPU inference cost into one-time storage cost — a direct margin lever.
insights.locator: To reduce serving overhead and prevent repeated calculations

insights.claim: The recommended operating rule is to query teachers online in early stages when teacher choices are still changing, then switch to offline caching once teachers stabilize and query volume increases.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: A transferable playbook for ML platform teams that decides when to pay compute versus storage.
insights.locator: Teams creating similar LLM-supervised ranking systems

themes.theme: Compounding training optimizations and the FP8 null result

insights.claim: The roughly eightfold training speedup comes from stacked optimizations — LiGer reducing memory to enable 2x larger batch sizes, multi-node training for up to 3.5x additional speedup, FSDP2 for a further 20%, and H200 multi-node clusters for up to 30% more.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Headline speedup claims decompose into moderate independent gains — useful for discounting single-vendor performance marketing.
insights.locator: That online/offline split sits alongside a broader stack

insights.claim: LinkedIn evaluated FP8 mixed precision and found no benefit for models under 8B parameters because casting overhead outweighed compute savings.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Undercuts the assumption that lower precision is a default win at small model sizes — relevant to hardware selection and NVIDIA's FP8 positioning.
insights.quote: The team notes it evaluated FP8 mixed precision but found no benefit for models under 8B parameters, due to casting overhead outweighing any compute savings.
insights.locator: The team notes it evaluated FP8 mixed precision

insights.claim: The gains from these optimizations are compounding rather than a single trick, with LiGer, multi-node data parallelism, FSDP2 and newer GPU generations each adding a moderate boost.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Argues ML infrastructure returns accrue through accumulated engineering, favouring teams with sustained platform investment.
insights.locator: The gains are compounding, not just one trick

insights.claim: A 0.6B-parameter student model distilled from an 8B relevance oracle and a 1.7B engagement teacher raised NDCG@10 for job searches by 24.48%, from 0.7583 to 0.9432.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: A sub-1B model delivering a 24% relevance gain shows frontier-scale inference is not required for high-value ranking.
insights.locator: On the modeling side, LinkedIn's research shows

insights.claim: Inference-side structured pruning and context compression increased ranking throughput from about 290 to over 2,000 items per second per GPU, roughly a sevenfold gain.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: 7x serving throughput per GPU is the number that makes LLM-based ranking economically viable at consumer scale.
insights.locator: Inference-side work in the same research included structured pruning

insights.claim: LinkedIn frames the work as a way to achieve cross-encoder-quality ranking while meeting real-time latency requirements and avoiding the high cost of using frontier-LLM inference for every request.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Large platforms are deliberately engineering away from per-request frontier inference — a structural cap on API revenue from high-volume products.
insights.locator: LinkedIn presents this work as a guide for teams

insights.claim: The system is live in production powering natural-language job search for LinkedIn's US users, not a research prototype.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Production deployment in a core revenue surface validates the distillation-over-frontier-inference economics.
insights.locator: The system is live in production

insights.claim: Many search and recommendation teams struggle to shift from keyword-based systems to unified rankers supervised by LLMs, making this a common industry transition rather than a LinkedIn-specific problem.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: A widespread migration in progress across search and recsys teams — sizeable demand for training and serving infrastructure.
insights.locator: Many search and recommendation teams face a common challenge

themes.theme: Industry comparison: Pinterest and frontier labs

insights.claim: Pinterest published a related account in June 2026 describing near-linear training scalability where multi-node training produced larger teacher models whose knowledge was distilled into efficient students for Homefeed and Related Pins ranking, cutting experimentation cycles from weeks to a fraction of that.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Two independent consumer platforms converging on teacher-student ranking confirms it as the dominant architecture for recsys.
insights.locator: In June 2026, Pinterest released a related account

insights.claim: Pinterest's emphasis is on scaling the training framework and migrating to Distributed Checkpoint to make multi-node teacher training possible, whereas LinkedIn's distinct contribution is a custom SGLang framework allowing teachers to be queried live during training.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Two divergent bets — checkpointing versus live serving — on the same problem; the winner sets the reference architecture.
insights.locator: Pinterest focuses on scaling the training framework

insights.claim: Frontier models including NVIDIA's Nemotron 3 Ultra, MiMo-V2-Flash and DeepSeek-V4 use ten or more specialized teachers for dense token-level supervision, a teacher-pool complexity that exceeds what industrial ranking systems like LinkedIn's and Pinterest's require.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Multi-teacher distillation is now standard at the frontier — a named list of models using it, and evidence the technique scales in both directions.
